review.summary: Phase 8 meets its acceptance criteria with real, source-bound, independently checkable evidence, and the three blocking/medium findings from attempt-03 are genuinely fixed rather than re-described. I re-derived the gate's command set from tools/check_phase.py (phase 1=7, 3=26, 4=29, 5=33, 6=36, 7=48, 8=77) and docs/checks/phase-08.json records exactly 77 commands, 77 `exit_code: 0`, `source_unchanged: true`, `passed: true`, and `source_sha256: 3d2c6caf…` equal to the reviewed source. The parity matrix is machine-enforced and fail-closed: tools/qualification.py:82-108 requires exactly 448 unique frozen operations with per-row export bindings, rejects constructor/non-method and family promotion, rejects any implementation/contract/option-parity gap, and raises on any unexplained gap; recorded output is operations 448, implemented 448, contractVerified 448, completeMethodOptionParity 448, liveVerified 17, unexplainedGaps 0. Live evidence is conservative and sanitized (17 verified methods, 3×403, 2×400 with cause explicitly unestablished and an SDK defect explicitly not excluded, cleanup `not_needed` because nothing was created), and tools/live_evidence.py re-binds the receipt to the current runtime fingerprint, closed vocabularies, and transport budget. Package checks are actual (archive extraction with member-safety and size limits, byte-identical LICENSE/NOTICE, packaged minimal/all-feature unit tests, doctests, example compilation, and the external 3,820-probe consumer on both 1.89.0 and 1.99.0), the dependency audit is fresh (RustSec 64f92cdc with freshHead true, pinned cargo-audit/cargo-deny with binary hashes, 206 packages, 0 vulnerabilities, no relaxable policy), platform labels are honest (musl native execution vs four compile-only targets with reqwest/tokio-websockets/rustls/aws-lc-rs proven absent from the target graphs), and the adversarial/parser corpus plus the 100×201 tracing stress run are real and reproducible. The attempt-03 CI findings are closed with verifiable artifacts: docs/CI.md now enumerates all four pinned actions with ls-remote-verified refs (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-actions.json), states that the action does set the runner default toolchain, corrects the runner prerequisites and Python floor/pin, a new guard (tools/test_ci.py:95-107) fails on the stale document and passes on the corrected one, and the delivery block/advisory are marked superseded with the clean-proof and push obligations reopened for this source. What keeps this at 9 rather than higher: the correction newly routes every CI job through a uv binary download whose available integrity control is unused, the "controlled live workflows and cleanup" milestone is only partially satisfied (no successful mutation or cleanup anywhere), the corrected workflow still has no remote execution receipt, and the clean-archive proofs and push for this source necessarily remain outstanding.

findings.description: The change under review adds a uv binary download to every CI job without using the integrity control the pinned action offers. The action's own recorded execution states "Checksum not provided. Checking known checksums." and "No known checksum found for x86_64-unknown-linux-musl-0.13.1" (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-uv-action.json:11), so in an actual run uv is fetched from GitHub releases with no digest verification; the pinned v6.6.0 manifest predates uv 0.13.1, so its known-checksum table cannot cover the pinned version on any platform. .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:45-50 passes only version/enable-cache/github-token even though the manifest declares a `checksum` input (.local/ci-bootstrap-2026-10-17/setup-uv-repository/action.yml:21-23), and the owned bootstrap only compares `uv --version` text, not the binary. The authoritative digests are already in the repository's own evidence (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-python-bootstrap.json:8-13 records archiveSha256 6c86040a… verified against the astral-sh/uv release API and binarySha256 752a98d0…), and docs/checks/phase-08-ci-uv-action.json:23 only asserts the match for the local exercise. docs/CI.md:54-62 discusses this residual trust for rustup but never states that the CI uv acquisition itself is unverified, while docs/phase-status.json:696 says the bootstrap used "hash-verified official uv 0.13.1", which is true only of the local run and is easy to read as covering CI.
findings.required_fix: Verify the uv executable in scripts/bootstrap-python.sh against a pinned per-platform SHA-256 table (hash `command -v uv` and fail closed on mismatch), and/or pass the action's `checksum` input for the single-platform jobs. Add a tools/test_ci.py guard asserting the pinned digest(s) and the uv version stay consistent, and state in docs/CI.md that the pinned action does not checksum-verify uv 0.13.1 and that the owned bootstrap now supplies that verification.

findings.description: Live mutation and cleanup workflows still have no successful service evidence. docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-06.json:212-242 shows iam.scopes.create and gateway.workspaces.provision rejected with 400 and rejectionDetails carrying no code and no field names, so the entire downstream chain (scope read/update/delete, absence verification, workspace archival and owned-binding cleanup) is unexercised live, and report `cleanup` is empty with cleanupState "not_needed" only because nothing was created. Milestone 8's "controlled live workflows and cleanup" is therefore only partly satisfied. This is recorded honestly as an experimental unqualified followup (docs/phase-status.json:624-633), the matrix keeps both operations at service_contract_rejection with the cause unestablished and an SDK request-shape defect explicitly not excluded (contracts/qualification.json:10747-10768, tools/qualification.py:27), and nothing is promoted on offline parity, so this is a scope limitation rather than a misrepresentation.
findings.required_fix: Keep both operations and every dependent mutation/cleanup path explicitly live-unqualified. Before any stable promotion, obtain private diagnostics for the two 400 responses, reconcile the traffic-derived IAM and Gateway provisioning request contracts against a vendor specification, and record a new source-bound receipt that exercises create/read/update/delete and confirmed cleanup.

findings.description: The delivered parity matrix records Rust paths inconsistently rooted: 194 of 448 rows carry the crate prefix (`"namespace": "scm_sdk::airs::gateway"` at line 2552) while 254 do not (`"airs::gateway"` at line 2687, `"dlp"`, `"shared::iam"`). The value is derived at tools/qualification.py:138 from rustMethods[0], which is assembled from free-text mapping namespaces at tools/native_operations.py:202, and validation only matches the final identifier against the source file (tools/native_exports.py:379-381), so the namespace portion of every recorded Rust path is unverified. The matrix is the headline phase-8 artifact, so `namespace` is not usable as a stable grouping key and rustMethods strings are not uniformly resolvable to real Rust items.
findings.required_fix: Normalize all mapping namespaces to one convention (either fully crate-rooted `scm_sdk::…` or consistently crate-relative) when building rustMethods in tools/native_operations.py:202, regenerate contracts/native-operations.json and contracts/qualification.json, and add an assertion in tools/test_native_operations.py that every rustMethods entry shares the chosen rooting and resolves to the recorded module path.

findings.description: The executed `native-probes` feature set still hardcodes the ten-feature union (agentguard, dlp, gateway, iam, management, model-security, models, red-team, realtime, scan). That currently equals the derived export-probe union asserted at tools/test_native_exports.py:121-129, but nothing asserts the two remain equal, so a future change to the generated union would silently leave the executed MSRV/current probe feature set behind. This is the still-open derived-probe-feature-drift-guard advisory (docs/phase-status.json:636-640).
findings.required_fix: Add an assertion (in tools/test_native_exports.py or tools/test_ci.py) that scripts/check-rust.py FEATURES["native-probes"] equals the derived requiredFeatures union in contracts/native-exports.json.

findings.description: The generated standalone public consumer declares its own `[workspace]`, so it does not inherit the repository's workspace-wide `unsafe_code = "forbid"` (Cargo.toml:12-13). The consumer source contains no unsafe code today and it is compiled and run from the extracted archive by scripts/check-package.py, but the policy is not enforced for it. This is the still-open consumer-unsafe-lint advisory (docs/phase-status.json:656-661).
findings.required_fix: Add `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"` to contracts/native-probes/Cargo.toml, or `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at the top of contracts/native-probes/src/main.rs, and regenerate the consumer.

findings.description: Two near-identically named documents still coexist: docs/LIVE-ACCEPTANCE.md (retained policy) and docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md (current execution and interpretation). Only the underscore form appears in docs/phase-status.json scope_evidence (line 531) and in README.md/RELEASE.md links, so the hyphen form is effectively unreferenced policy prose that is easy to mis-edit or mis-link. Attempt-03 raised this as a low finding; unlike the other attempt-03 lows it was neither fixed nor recorded as an advisory in docs/phase-status.json, so the review-disposition ledger is incomplete for it.
findings.required_fix: Merge docs/LIVE-ACCEPTANCE.md into docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md as a policy section, or rename it to docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE_POLICY.md and update inbound references; either way record the disposition in docs/phase-status.json review_advisories.

findings.description: The correction record understates the change in one field while disclosing it in others. `verification_scope` says the gate was rerun "after attempt-03 documentation fixes", but the reviewed source also replaced the CI Python provisioning mechanism: the attempt-03 source (e5903a90…) used actions/setup-python, whereas this source uses astral-sh/setup-uv plus the new owned scripts/bootstrap-python.sh (disclosed in `scope` at line 687, `review_context` at line 711 and the `portable_python` block at lines 746-759, and corroborated by docs/checks/phase-08-python-bootstrap-transition.json:2-9). Relatedly, milestones.implemented_scope.evidence (lines 568-576) lists ci.yml, .python-version, docs/CI.md, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and tools/test_ci.py but omits scripts/bootstrap-python.sh and .gitattributes, which are the newly added owned artifacts of this correction.
findings.required_fix: Reword verification_scope to state that the reviewed source changed both the CI Python provisioning mechanism and the documentation, and add scripts/bootstrap-python.sh and .gitattributes to milestones.implemented_scope.evidence.

findings.description: The corrected workflow still has no execution receipt. The local exercises install rustup directly and run the pinned uv action and bootstrap script outside any runner, and PATH-file application is simulated (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-python-bootstrap.json:80-84, docs/checks/phase-08-ci-uv-action.json:17-20), so the fix's effectiveness on a real runner — the action's $GITHUB_PATH export, `--offline` cargo cache coverage for the separate contracts/native-probes lockfile, and the 180-minute cold-cache budget for the 77-command gate — remains unverified. Likewise the reviewed source is uncommitted, origin/main is still 4f65dc48, and the only --require-clean archive proofs bind releaseCommit f4178928. All of this is labeled honestly (docs/phase-status.json:546-564, docs/CI.md:101-119, docs/RELEASE.md:74-75) and the push/proof step must by construction follow this review, so it is an outstanding delivery obligation rather than a misstatement.
findings.required_fix: Keep remote_ci at "configured_unexecuted" until a Forgejo run log for the corrected workflow (at minimum contracts-and-package and one rust matrix job) is retained. Before marking phase 8 complete, commit the reviewed source, run both --require-clean archive checks on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 with distinct ignored outputs, push the ordinary commits, and record the exact commit plus both archive digests and a refreshed private-material scan.

crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs:25-195 implements the reserved-protocol-key guard with explicit 512 MiB byte, 128 depth, 1,000,000 node and 4×length work bounds, handles escaped (\uXXXX and ordinary) key spellings at lines 68-111, and guard_value at 197-255 uses an explicit iterator stack so rejecting a deep caller-created Value cannot recurse; grepping the crate shows every non-test use of serde_json::from_slice/from_str/from_value is inside json_decode.rs itself, so the boundary is actually centralized rather than merely documented.

docs/checks/phase-08-tracing-stress-1.99.0.json records 100 processes × 201 passing tests at 16 threads bound to sourceSha256, runtimeInputsSha256 and binarySha256; tools/test_auxiliary_evidence.py:351-437 proves the stress runner fails closed on source, runtime, binary or build drift, on any changed per-process summary, and on the total deadline, and that its report write is atomic, 0600, non-overwriting and symlink-refusing.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/parser_qualification.rs plus docs/ADVERSARIAL.md:14-37 document and bound the executed corpus (384 exhaustive short-frame partitions, 2,048 seeded mutations across four fixed seeds run contiguously and in 1-13-byte chunks, malformed UTF-8 and truncation at every two-chunk split, frame/size boundaries, lifecycle terminals, overflow fail-closed envelopes, and cancellation/drop/transport-error latching without replay), and explicitly disclaims being a coverage-guided fuzzer.

docs/STABILITY.md:11-25 keeps Implemented, Offline contracts verified, Live accepted, Platform qualified and Released as separate claims and states that a denied permission or blocked service never becomes a passing live result; README.md:16-20 states the crate is not published and no retained remote CI execution is claimed; docs/RELEASE.md:29-57 and 74-75 describe the clean-commit archive proof and remote CI status as outstanding. Cargo.toml:12-13 sets workspace `unsafe_code = "forbid"` and crates/scm-sdk/src/lib.rs repeats `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

docs/phase-status.json:546-564 now records delivery status "ci_correction_awaiting_current_review_clean_commit_proof_and_push" with source_commit null, source_pushed false, source_sha256 3d2c6caf…, clean_release_archive "pending_for_corrected_reviewed_source" with empty proofs, the superseded f4178928 delivery moved to historical_deliveries, the clean-commit-proof-and-push advisory reopened (lines 662-672), and milestones.independent_verification.source_sha256 (line 582) equal to the hash recorded inside the cited docs/checks/phase-08.json — the three attempt-03 findings are therefore closed, not restated.
limitations: I had read-only Read/Glob/Grep and no shell or hashing tool, so I could not compute any SHA-256. I could not confirm that docs/checks/phase-08.json hashes to db481b80d3e185030298699a0817381f0ea87aaf8dd47d4356903d9d8908fafa, nor recompute the reviewed source fingerprint; I verified instead that the report's self-recorded source_sha256 equals the reviewed source in the prompt and that its command list matches the gate binding in tools/check_phase.py. For the same reason I could not confirm that docs/checks/phase-08-ci-regression.json's corrected-workflow inputSha256 (6a77cc76…) is the current .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml, only that its asserted content matches what the current workflow and document contain.

I re-executed nothing. All Rust, package, cross, dependency, tracing-stress, CI-bootstrap and live results are read from recorded reports; I verified their internal consistency, command lines, source/runtime/binary bindings and the fail-closed logic of the runner scripts, not their re-reproducibility.

No remote CI execution evidence exists for the corrected workflow, so my judgment that the bootstrap fix resolves the reported exit 127 and that the new uv/Python path works on a Forgejo runner rests on the pinned action manifests, the offline workflow guards and the local exercises, not on an observed runner run. The $GITHUB_PATH export and non-Linux-x86_64 behavior remain unverified.

I did not read any credential or tenant-registration file and made no network calls, so the live receipt's service interactions are assessed only through the sanitized allowlisted report and the verifier's rejection logic. I cannot independently establish whether the two 400 responses are service-contract or SDK request-shape defects; the record explicitly declines to exclude either.

I did not audit all 448 operation rows, all 3,820 export capabilities, or the full Rust source tree. For contract completeness I relied on the fail-closed generators and their tamper tests (tools/test_qualification.py, test_native_operations.py, test_native_exports.py, verify-contracts.py --self-test) plus targeted spot checks of gateway realtime/chat-completion, provisioning and IAM rows and of the JSON decoding boundary.

I inspected the cached pinned action manifests under .local/ci-bootstrap-2026-10-17/, which docs/phase-status.json and docs/checks/phase-08-ci-actions.json declare as nonsecret read-only references inside the repository; I did not verify that those cached copies match the upstream commits beyond their recorded hashes.

The score reflects this phase's criteria only. The pre-existing phase-2/4 limitations now marked resolved, and the earlier phases' accepted records, were checked only where phase 8 artifacts cite them.
